title: Patrick Dougherty: How to Build AI Agents that Actually Work
talk_summary: Patrick Dougherty (ex-CTO of Rosco) shares lessons from rebuilding a product around AI agents: favor reasoning over stuffing knowledge into prompts, iterate hard on the agent-computer interface (tool call syntax and response formats), avoid fine-tuning and heavy frameworks, and structure multi-agent systems as a manager plus 5-8 workers incentivized on the outcome.

takeaways.technique: Discrete retrieval tools instead of giant context dumps
takeaways.what_they_do: Rather than injecting all schema/data into the system prompt (RAG-style), they expose small retrieval tools (search tables, get table detail, profile a column) and let the agent iteratively pull only what it needs.
takeaways.numbers: cited failure with 500-1000 column tables returning ~30,000 tokens of context

takeaways.what_they_do: They iterated on the exact format of tool call inputs/outputs per model: switching search results from markdown to JSON fixed GPT-4o missing columns, while Claude needed XML instead of JSON.

takeaways.technique: Cheap models for subtasks, strong model for the decision step
takeaways.what_they_do: They allow cheaper models for tool calls/sub-prompts but insist the model deciding the next tool call be a generally intelligent one, because that decision drives the whole trajectory.

takeaways.technique: Reward 'I can't do this' over forced output
takeaways.what_they_do: They contrast GPT-4o (always writes a query even when impossible) with o1 (correctly concludes the schema can't answer the question), and argue agents should be allowed/encouraged to report missing data instead of fabricating.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if it doesn't find it it should be able to tell you that it didn't find it and you can take some action with that knowledge

takeaways.what_they_do: A manager agent owns the final outcome and delegates to specialized workers with narrower context/tools; teams are capped around 5-8 agents, and the manager is incentivized on the objective rather than forced through fixed steps.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you could limit yourself to about between five and eight agents working together then that was typically a task that could be accomplished well
takeaways.numbers: 5-8 agents per team; 25-50 agent systems cited as prone to infinite loops

takeaways.technique: Read hallucinated tool args as ACI feedback
takeaways.what_they_do: When a model consistently ignores the JSON schema and emits args in another format, they treat that as the model telling you how the tool should be defined and reshape the tool to match.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you see it consistently ignoring your Json schema for a tool call and providing an argument in a different format that should be an indicator to you
